constraint_findings.finding: The 600 V reference candidate does not satisfy the retained design's implied transient contract (1000 V-class bridge, no declared surge clamp), nor NXP's own 700 V node limit; it satisfies only an added-clamp contract limiting the bridge node to <=500 V.

The high-side gate-source voltage is ~8.5 V typical, not Vregd 10.7 V; the 10 V Rds(on) data is not directly applicable to the high side. The penalty is small for this die (~2%), but grows if the bootstrap capacitor is undersized (100 nF -> ~7.3 V).
The IPW60R017C7 body diode is slow (Qrr typ 18 uC at 58.2 A/400 V); a fast-body-diode device may be required for the active bridge, which would change Rds(on) and the saving.

answer: CONDITIONAL YES on losses, CONDITIONAL on voltage rating. With the real bootstrap-derived high-side gate bias (~8.5 V) and a COMPUTED steady-state Tj of ~45-46 C in the proposed four-TO-247 heatsink assembly, the reference IPW60R017C7 conducts at ~17.2-17.6 mOhm per device and saves ~15-27 W (nominal ~20.5 W) against the 23-35 W bridge bracket, before the unquantified inrush/EMI terms. However, the 600 V device does not satisfy the retained design's implied transient contract (a 1000 V-class bridge with no declared surge clamp); it is valid only if an added clamp limits the bridge node to <=500 V. A lower-voltage alternative is not supported by the contract and was not screened.

single_missing_input.input: The product's real input transient/surge contract (test level and whether a front-end clamp is fitted).
single_missing_input.why: It is the only input that decides whether a 600 V-class device may be used at all. The loss result is already robust and favourable (~15-27 W saved at a computed 45-46 C junction), but it is gated: with no declared clamp and a retained 1000 V-class bridge, the reference candidate's 600 V rating is unsupported, and every lower-voltage alternative is excluded outright.
